tools_used: subagent read of petition and BIOs
helpful: Provisioned merits brief text (petitioner) and the statpack merits table with explicit excluded counts
documents.json entry dates, which exposed that the 'respondent' brief was filed by an aligned party
gaps: No provisioned text for the other same-day merits briefs (United States, legislative leaders); one row per side drops the amicus-like respondents in a multi-sided case
A side-alignment field on provisioned briefs (supporting petitioner / respondent / neither) would have saved a close read to discover the partial-support posture
CourtListener opinion/cluster records for the Ninth Circuit decision carried no panel or author fields, so the lower-court lineup had to come from the filings
No committed base rate for the judgment label mix (reversed vs vacated vs in-part) or for vote splits
notes: The corpus query surface was not useful for a merits cell: the citation column is sparse and the ranked priors are cert-stage shapes. The statpack merits table did the anchoring work.
